plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a dual-bandpass filter design using recalled IR coating principles without any literature retrieval. The approach uses a high/low index pair (ZnS/Al2O3) in a fixed 22-layer alternating structure with individually tunable layer thicknesses to create transmission peaks at 3.3 μm and 4.25 μm while suppressing adjacent bands. This route relies entirely on prior knowledge of thin-film interference physics and common IR dielectric materials. Previous iteration failed with ZnS/MgF2 due to material_data issues; this revision switches to ZnS/Al2O3 with explicit thickness bounds and preprocessing validation. Substrate material name repaired to resolve registry ambiguity.

routes.title: Dual-bandpass IR filter with ZnS/Al2O3 alternating stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer alternating high-low index stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve simultaneous transmission peaks at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm while suppressing 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm bands on CaF2 substrate.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack physics: alternating high and low refractive index layers create constructive and destructive interference at design wavelengths. By tuning individual layer thicknesses away from strict quarter-wave values, multiple passbands can be engineered through controlled phase relationships across the stack. Higher index contrast yields broader stopbands.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | Daimon-20
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.20-4.30 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.45-5.00 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
All materials are conventional depositable dielectrics
Individual layer thicknesses bounded to 50-1500 nm for practical deposition
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength; deviation from quarter-wave can create transmission windows at other wavelengths
Recalled: ZnS has high refractive index (approximately 2.3-2.4) in mid-IR range and is commonly used for IR coatings
Recalled: Al2O3 has lower refractive index (approximately 1.6-1.7) and is transparent in mid-IR, commonly used as low-index counterpart
Recalled: Dual-bandpass filters typically require non-uniform thickness optimization rather than strict periodicity
Recalled: CaF2 substrate is transparent in 2.5-5.0 μm range and is suitable for IR applications
Recalled: Index contrast between high and low materials determines stopband width and depth
expected_advantages: ZnS/Al2O3 pair provides sufficient index contrast for effective interference in mid-IR
22 layers allows enough degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization while staying under 24-layer limit
Individual thickness tuning enables control over both passband positions and stopband suppression
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard deposition techniques
known_risks: Uncertain whether ZnS and Al2O3 material data extends fully to 5.0 μm in the registry - previous iteration failed with ZnS/MgF2 citing material_data issues; need to verify n/k values are finite across 2.5-5.0 μm

Uncertain optimal starting thickness values - quarter-wave at 3.3 μm would be approximately 350-400 nm for ZnS and 500-550 nm for Al2O3 based on recalled indices, but dual-band requires compromise between 3.3 μm and 4.25 μm
Periodic alternating structure may not be optimal for dual-bandpass; a more complex topology with defect layers or multiple cavities might be needed but would change the axis
22 layers may not provide enough design freedom for two well-separated passbands with good suppression - this is a hypothesis to test
What would settle material uncertainty: Check material catalog for actual wavelength coverage of zns and al2o3 datasets; verify n/k arrays contain finite floats across full 2500-5000 nm range
What would settle topology question: Compare against routes using different stack architectures (e.g., cavity-based designs)
Substrate material name ambiguity resolved by selecting Daimon-20 dataset; uncertainty remains whether this specific dataset has complete coverage across 2.5-5.0 μm
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer multilayer optical filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Stack sequence from air side: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 layers total, alternating starting with ZnS, ending with Al2O3 (Kischkat) on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate). Optimize individual layer thicknesses for each of the 22 layers independently. Thickness bounds: 50 nm minimum, 1500 nm maximum per layer. Target behavior: high transmittance at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm; low transmittance at 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm. No metal layers. Materials: zns and Al2O3 (Kischkat) from catalog. Substrate: CaF2 (Daimon-20). Incidence: air to stack. Evaluate transmittance and reflectance across 2500-5000 nm wavelength range.
routes.revision_reason: Previous iteration failed with ZnS/MgF2 pair due to material_data issues (zero physically valid candidates). This revision switches to ZnS/Al2O3 pair with explicit thickness bounds (50-1500 nm) to ensure physical validity. Added preprocessing validation requirement for refractive index arrays to contain finite floats before TMM evaluation. Substrate material name repaired from ambiguous 'CaF2' to specific dataset 'Daimon-20' to resolve registry ambiguity. Maintains same control route identity for comparison purposes.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all material pair combinations and topology variations fail to produce valid candidates with positive target scores, the problem may require non-planar geometry, different material system outside the catalog, relaxation of layer count constraint, or acceptance that the specified bands cannot be achieved simultaneously with conventional dielectric stacks under these constraints.

expected_observations: If hypothesis holds: best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as thicknesses converge toward dual-bandpass solution
If hypothesis holds: valid_candidates count should be greater than zero after thickness bounds are enforced and material data validated
If hypothesis holds: tightest_margin should remain stable or improve across rounds indicating physical constraints are satisfiable
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score remains near zero indicating the periodic topology cannot achieve dual-bandpass with this material pair
If hypothesis fails: valid_candidates remains zero indicating material data issues persist with ZnS/Al2O3 in this wavelength range
If hypothesis fails: tightest_margin decreases across rounds indicating physical constraints cannot be satisfied simultaneously
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates remains zero for three consecutive rounds despite thickness bound adjustments and material validation, stop and flag material pair as incompatible with this topology
If tightest_margin falls below zero for three consecutive rounds, stop and indicate the constraint set is infeasible for this stack architecture

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
